Everything on one screen

A single static reference — purpose, stack, data flow, model pipeline, file layout, and I/O — for a fast pass before diving into the interactive pages.

Purpose

Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction for aircraft turbofan engines, built entirely on PyTorch, benchmarked on NASA's C-MAPSS engine degradation dataset.

PyTorch pandas / NumPy scikit-learn (benchmark + metrics) Python 3.9+
Input → Output
(30, 21) sensor window per engine, standardized
→
model(x) MLP / CNN / LSTM / GRU / RF
→
RUL (cycles) scalar, capped at 125

No deployment/inference script is included in the repository — the notebook covers training and offline evaluation only.

Data flow
01Download & extract → 02Load into DataFrames → 03EDA: missing values & constant sensors → 04Engineer the RUL label → 05Engine-grouped train/val split → 06Standardize features → 07Slide a window per engine → 08Dataset & DataLoader → 09Prepare the official test set
Model pipeline
MLP Flatten → Linear → ReLU → Linear → ReLU → Linear 1D-CNN Conv1d → ReLU → Conv1d → ReLU → AdaptiveAvgPool1d → Linear LSTM LSTM(batch_first=True) → Linear on the final hidden state GRU GRU(batch_first=True) → Linear on the final hidden state Random Forest RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, max_depth=10)
Hyperparameters
WINDOW_SIZE30 cycles
RUL_CAP125 cycles
BATCH_SIZE64
EPOCHS10
LR1e-3
Train/val split80% / 20%, grouped by engine
Random seed42
